name: Fox Trot
beta: Climb the huecos up to a pair of cracks, which take wires, small cams and camming units up to about 1.5 inches.
overview: Huecos lead to a pair of cracks. Rated among the best routes in the park.

current.descent: 2-rope rappel
current.detailed_rack: wires, TCUs and cams up to 1.5 in
current.location: six feet along from Head Fox, to its right

name: French Route
beta: Easy ground angling leftward leads onto a little ledge; go straight up past three bolts to a gap of the overhanging arch, clip the bolt above, then ascend a rib on solid holds toward a flake that takes gear, and finish on the upper ledges.
overview: An enjoyable, thin slab that uses a whole rope length. Easy ground left to a ledge, three bolts straight above into a break of the leaning arch, then a bold run on solid holds along a rib toward a protectable flake and onward to upper ledges.

current.area_walk_in: Take the Echo Canyon trail through the saddle between Main Dome and Little Dome, drop down the draw and cross the boulders, then follow the trail that loops around the dome to the wall's base.
current.descent: rappel from anchors to the right

name: Dungeons and Dragons
beta: Start from a block at the floor of the slot and follow the gently overhanging rock, clipping two bolts and placing gear in several slots, with a horn you can loop with a sling; a third bolt covers the final stretch.
overview: A well-hidden climb launching from a boulder inside a chimney, working up gently overhanging rock with bolts, nut and cam placements and a horn that can be looped.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.location: at the base of the chimney, launching from a boulder

name: Hueco Syndrome
beta:
First pitch: start a few feet to the pillars' left and follow five bolts directly up to the belay.

Second pitch: ascend the shallow dihedral overhead, following bolts upward, then traverse rightward fifteen feet onto easy ground and finish on solid holds.
overview: The first pitch goes directly up five bolts to a bolted belay. The second climbs a shallow dihedral that faces left, with bolts, then shifts right 15 ft onto easy ground and finishes on good holds.

current.location: six feet from the Uriah's Heap pillars on their left

name: Little Feat
beta: Hand-jamming on sound rock gives way to lower-angled ground; set aside a couple of large cams, roughly three to three-and-a-half inches, for the belay.
overview: Solid hand jams on the lower section lead to easier-angled rock above. Described as a quality line; the belay is built from gear.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.detailed_rack: reserve a few 3-3.5 in cams for the belay
current.location: extreme right-hand limit of the east wall

name: Lunacy
beta:
First pitch: stem up the corner for about 75 feet until a small roof appears, get over it and continue up a section of finger crack to a ledge with a two-bolt belay.

Second pitch: head for the large roof holding a wide crack, force a way through, then climb the chimney above to the top.
overview: An obvious corner system holding a wide crack, giving beautiful, sustained stemming. The second pitch goes through a big roof and into a chimney.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Lunar Abstract
beta: Follow the narrow, steep crack-and-seam that splits the right-hand face of the Lunacy corner; lower off the two-bolt anchor or continue by joining Lunatic Friends.
overview: A thin overhanging seam of a crack set in the right side of the corner that Lunacy climbs. Lower from the bolted anchor or link into Lunatic Friends.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: optical promise
beta: Traverse right from the belay to a sloping ledge beneath the overhanging rock. Then climb the face protected by three bolts as far as a crack, which needs its own gear and the anchors.
overview: Steep, airy climbing that begins from a ledge reached via the neighbouring route. The top pitch follows a line of holds up and right into a crack through overhanging rock, with bolts on the face below it.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Rainbow Bridge
beta:
First pitch: a thin section of face trends up and rightward to a right-slanting flake system; follow that flake line into the large arching dihedral, step across into it and finish via the crack to a belay.

Second pitch: move right off the belay onto a dark rib and follow good holds directly up for about fifty feet to a big scooped ledge.

Final pitch: from the belay step right and head straight to a bolt, shift rightward to a hands-free rest, then a second bolt, pause there, then reach the little bulge, traversing leftward below it.
overview: First pitch angles right up a flake system that faces left to the arching dihedral, then a 5.9 crack. The middle pitch is easy on good holds. The finale is a wild overhanging buttress.

current.location: perched on large blocks lower down, off to Indecent Exposure's right

name: Runamuck
beta: Share Edge of Night's start, friction up to a slender arch angling rightward, follow it with small gear to its finish, then ascend a shallow corner demanding commitment directly to the summit.
overview: Shares its opening with Edge of Night, then friction to a thin arch that slants rightward; after the arch ends, a shallow corner with a committing feel leads to the top.

current.area_walk_in: Take the Echo Canyon trail through the saddle between Main Dome and Little Dome, drop down the draw and cross the boulders, then follow the trail that loops around the dome to the wall's base.

name: Sixth Happiness
beta: Get beyond the arch and clip a bolt, keep going straight up thin ground past two more bolts, then higher make a hard traverse leftward to the fifth bolt of Texas Radio and finish up easier ground to the belay.
overview: A hard, bold lead: surmount the arch for a bolt, climb thin ground with two more bolts, then cross a scary leftward traverse to a fifth bolt on the neighbouring route. Easy 5.7 for 60 ft then reaches the belay.

current.area_walk_in: Take the Echo Canyon trail through the saddle between Main Dome and Little Dome, drop down the draw and cross the boulders, then follow the trail that loops around the dome to the wall's base.

name: Son of Cakewalk
beta:
First pitch: begin close to the hourglass shape, just beyond it on the right, climb up to a little roof beside a corner, get over it, and head directly up on superb holds until a crack, and belay there.

Second pitch: keep following the crack up toward a stubby headwall, and reach the top by stepping across the chockstone wedged in the crevice, or descend into the crevice by rappel.
overview: Pitch one gets past a small roof near a dihedral that faces left, then runs directly up superb holds toward a crack with a belay about 150 ft off the ground. Pitch two stays on that crack up to a short steep step; finish by crossing the jammed block in the gap up top, or lower into the gap.

current.descent: walk off toward Laguna Prieta
current.location: ten feet beyond the hourglass-like feature, rightward

name: Stranger Than Friction
beta: Begin atop the flake, shift up and leftward into a concave dish with a bolt, work leftward to a tough mantel, then trend up and rightward past further bolts to the belay. An easy short slab pitch then leads to the summit.
overview: Described as a popular classic with good protection. Leaving the flake summit, angle leftward to a scooped dish with a bolt, continue left to a stiff mantle, then head rightward clipping further bolts, finishing with an easy 35 ft runout to the belay. A brief easy slab leads to the summit.

current.area_walk_in: Take the Echo Canyon trail through the saddle between Main Dome and Little Dome, drop down the draw and cross the boulders, then follow the trail that loops around the dome to the wall's base.

name: Terminal Orogeny
beta: Go up a flake that accepts small cams or nuts onto a crystalline face with a bolt, then cross the arch overhead to another bolt and trend up leftward to the belay of Stranger Than Friction.
overview: A flake takes gear en route to a crystalline face with a bolt; keep going above the arch to a second bolt, then slant left to the belay used by the neighbouring route.

current.area_walk_in: Take the Echo Canyon trail through the saddle between Main Dome and Little Dome, drop down the draw and cross the boulders, then follow the trail that loops around the dome to the wall's base.

name: Texas Crude
beta: Follow the overhanging hand crack up to a ledge, where mid-size gear handles both the placements en route and the belay anchor.
overview: An overhanging hand crack, rated excellent, that leads up to a ledge where the belay is made.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.detailed_rack: medium-size gear for protection and belay
current.location: the leftmost of three cracks, on the section of wall past the big dihedral

name: True Grip
beta:
First pitch: work the corner at the far right of Flake Roof up to a little roof, stem left, cross a gentler huecoed face beside a bush toward a horizontal crack, then shift leftward then upward to the belay bolts.

Second pitch: head across leftward to a bolt, continue up and leftward until a horizontal crack, then pull through steep ground with big huecos (the crux) over another horizontal crack to the summit.
overview: A good two-pitch line on the headwall over Flake Roof. The first pitch works a corner then a gentler face full of huecos; the second sweeps up steeper rock with big huecos, where the crux lies.

current.descent: walk off north over the slabs

name: Walking on the Moon
beta: From the juniper beside the start, pull a short bulge to a bolt-protected tiered ledge, clip a second bolt about ten feet higher, then veer up-left to a thin vertical crack that takes a wired nut. After that, trend right and up toward a modest corner, get past it and belay.
overview: A hair-raising line. Pull a brief overhang onto a stepped ledge holding a bolt, clip a second bolt ten feet above, then drift left toward a narrow upright crack roughly 100 ft off the ground. Next angle right to a little dihedral that faces left, go over it, and belay at Final Stone.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)
current.detailed_rack: a wired nut for the small vertical crack
current.location: at the tree beside Purple Microdot, next to a big juniper

name: William's Lectric Shave
beta: Start by stepping off the small immovable rock sitting at the base of the face.
overview: A line up a thin, sharp-edged face close to the prow, on its right.

current.descent: (no DESCENT section on this route's page)

name: Window Pain
beta: Start from a ramp neighbouring Lunacy on its left, go up and leftward to a ledge-like stance over a little roof, then follow steep rock with lots of bolts leading to a comfy belay ledge.
overview: Climb up and leftward to a stance over a small roof, then follow steep rock, well bolted, up to a good belay ledge.

current.descent: rappel with two ropes from the belay ledge
current.location: on a ramp left of Lunacy

name: A Visit From Juan
beta: Climb past four bolts, after which the slab gets much easier all the way up.
overview: Four bolts protect the harder opening; after that the route relaxes onto far easier slab, with long gaps between protection.

current.area_walk_in: Descend from the Ridge Trail beside the Whale's Lip wall, quit its descent path after about 50 yards, and bushwhack rightward around a small outcrop. Drop down the vegetated slope for around 100 yards until a corridor between huge blocks appears on your right. Walk through it to the foot of the big slab.

name: Alchemy
beta: Climb the arete and the face on its right past four bolts to a horizontal crack, then move rightward and complete the climb via a crack.
overview: The arete and the face to its right lead up on bolts to a sideways crack, after which you move right and follow another crack out.

current.area_walk_in: Leave the main ridge path at the clearing and slab that face east; where a path forks at the slab's bottom, bear right and keep going directly through the trees. About 75 yards on, a cluster of rock outcrops appears, and the routes sit on one east-facing wall.

name: Almond Joy
beta: The line ascends the grey, slab-like face as far as a tree; from there a leftward scramble along a ledge reaches the anchors of a neighbouring route.
overview: Meander up the grey wall as far as a tree, then step left along a ledge to the anchors.

name: Alpenglow
beta: Start by bouldering up some blocks onto the left of the orange face, work rightward along a horizontal slot to the bolt sitting on the prow, then proceed directly above clipping four more.
overview: Classic. From the blocks, work rightward along a sideways break until a bolt appears at the nose, then go straight up on four more.

name: Autumn Harvest
beta:
Begin from a little detached block at the face's left, trend upward and rightward, clipping a bolt on the way to a tiny overlap (a good gear spot), then keep going directly upward by two further bolts to a flake and gentler slab finishing.

Carry a slim rack of modest-sized cams and stoppers.
overview: A nice climb. Angle rightward beside a bolt up to a minor overlap where gear can go in, then head directly upward, clipping two further bolts, to a flake (facing left) and gentler slab moves up top.

name: Bermuda Triangle
beta: Follow the thin crack as it slants leftward, then the small corner above, up to the triangular roof where anchors sit on the right.
overview: A thin, slanting crack that leads into a small corner and ends at a triangular roof.

beta: Walk up the ramp, then ascend the right-hand crack.
overview: Takes the right-hand of a pair of side-by-side cracks splitting an overhanging wall, reached via a ramp; its neighbour Cranko takes the left crack.

name: Dark Side of the Moon
beta: Start from the chockstone sitting at the Frigid Air dihedral's foot, boulder up and rightward onto the wall, follow the bolt line slanting rightward, then curve back toward the left along a gentle arete to the anchors.
overview: Good face climbing on the shady wall that looks north. Bolts trending rightward lead up, then the route curls back toward the left on a gently angled arete to the anchors.

beta: Begin in the wide fissure on the right-hand side of the gully, then finish on the gentler face above, clipping two bolts.
overview: The route opens with that offwidth, then eases onto a gentler face where two bolts protect the finish.

beta: Begin behind a tree by the left wall, work through fragile crystal-edge moves past three bolts, reaching a horizontal slot that takes gear, then finish over simpler ground to a tree.
overview: Delicate crystal-edge moves lead past bolts to a sideways break that takes gear, then easier rock leads to a tree.

name: Entropy
beta: From around ten feet beyond some ancient bolts, ascend the flake into a minor overhang, then move leftward to end on a large flake that faces right.
overview: A flake leads to a little roof; shift leftward there and top out on a large flake facing right.

beta: Layback the wide crack in the dominant inside corner to anchors by the left wall; larger cams (medium and up) are what you need.

name: Ganja
beta: Climb easy rock, clipping a bolt, onto a ledge, then power up the pale streak with four bolts to the anchors.
overview: Short, brawny and well regarded. Easy ground gets you to a ledge, and the fireworks start on a pale streak above.

name: God Knows
beta:
Begin on slab at the briar shelf's far-left end, aiming for a first bolt that sits high; above, the nose steepens and offers five more bolts leading to a horizontal break, from which a rightward traverse reaches the anchors of another route.

Using a stick-clip for the lofty initial bolt is wise, and a few cams protect the traverse.
overview: Slabby rock gets you up to a lofty first bolt, then a steeper nose continues until a sideways crack allows a shift rightward to the anchors. Clipping the first bolt with a stick and carrying a few cams for the traverse is advised. A pleasant route overall.

beta: Follow the bolt line slanting leftward up the south-facing wall, which is steep.
overview: Classic. A line of bolts drifting leftward climbs the steep wall that looks south, said to be arguably the finest 5.11 face route on the mountain.

name: Microdigits
beta: Start in a slender crack that kinks sharply leftward about ten feet up, work it until a decent horizontal hold, then finish on easier ground, or traverse over leftward a short way and descend Doublecrack.
overview: The thin crack is followed as far as a solid horizontal hold, and easier moves lead to the top. Alternatively, step a short distance leftward and descend Doublecrack.

name: House Broken
beta: Work a gentle hand crack along the gully's left side until it ends, then shift left and keep climbing the nose to the anchors.
overview: A hand crack of gentle angle runs until it peters out, after which you step left and finish on the nose, reaching the anchors.

name: Introspection
beta: Start in a corner that opens rightward and boulder through steep sequences up to a stance beneath bolt number one; friction on to bolt number two, drift a bit right, then run to a flake and horizontal slot. Complete the route on the face overhead past one more bolt.
overview: Follows an unmistakable line of bolts with homemade hangers up the center of the wall. Friction across to bolt two, drift a little right, then dash to a flake (facing right) and a horizontal crack, finishing on the face above with one more bolt.
